rows.b: A resistive-memory array performs neural-network math where the weights live, beside a small digital controller. Data barely moves, so power plummets.
A future computer that never erases information, dodging the fundamental heat limit of logic. It would run cool forever, in principle. SPECULATION: only lab demos exist.
A computer built on the free and open RISC-V instruction set, so anyone can study and build on its design. It runs Linux and standard software.
Logic gates from a superconductor that works at room temperature would switch at enormous speed with no cooling at all. SPECULATION: no verified room-temperature superconductor exists.
Atoms puffed up to huge Rydberg states interact powerfully over long distances, making fast quantum gates. Laser tweezers place each atom exactly where the problem needs it.
